the_identity.graphic_mark: yes — the sidebar draws an inline <svg> brand mark on every page (index.html, span.brand-logo): a rounded tile, a five-point star, a dot beneath it
the_identity.so: nothing was drawn or invented. The mark was copied, the way egod's was — no letter had to be traced, unlike chizukim and orech.

measured_from_the_live_page_not_from_css.path_d: copied verbatim from the nav svg, not redrawn
measured_from_the_live_page_not_from_css.corner: rx/side of the original tile is 9/34 = 0.2647, which is 12.71 in a 48 box

the_identity.geometry_is_a_mapping_not_a_choice: the original mark's content lives inside its own rounded rect, (3,3)→(37,37) of a 40 viewBox. That 34-box is mapped onto the full 48 box — scale 48/34 = 1.4118, translate −4.235 — so the star-to-tile ratio in the tab is exactly the ratio on the page. No number was picked by eye.

deviation_declared_in_the_file: in the nav the tile is gold at 12% opacity over the sidebar's teal; here the tile is that teal itself. In a tab there is no sidebar underneath to take the colour from, and a 12% wash is not visible at 16px anyway. This is the only change to the mark.
the_trap_from_the_previous_round_was_avo: orech shipped a favicon that returned 200 at the right byte count and painted nothing, because the Hebrew comment documented tokens as var(--…) and two consecutive hyphens are illegal inside an XML comment. This file writes token names without their var() wrapper and says why, and decode is asserted separately from status.

verified_on_a_real_render.how: scripts/qa/serve-smachot.mjs serves _deploy/smachot-more30 the way Vercel does — /smachot/ is a real directory inside the deploy root, and the root itself is empty so origin fallbacks 404. Then a real Chromium load of /smachot/.
verified_on_a_real_render.not_grep: the assertions are the resolved href in the live DOM and the bytes the browser got back — not a string in a source file
verified_on_a_real_render.resolved_via: the <base href="/smachot/"> already in the document — the relative href is deliberate, it is what makes the path survive the mount
verified_on_a_real_render.screenshot: sizes.png beside this file — 16/32/64/192 on a light tab strip, a dark tab strip, and both of smachot's own tones

measured_on_the_16px_raster.why: a five-point star is the shape most likely to turn into a blob at 16px
measured_on_the_16px_raster.star: rows 3-10, widest 8px on row 6; the two lower arms are still separated by tile on row 10
measured_on_the_16px_raster.dot: row 13, 2px wide — it survives as a mark, not as a shape
measured_on_the_16px_raster.star_peak: exact rgb(230,183,61), i.e. full gold-soft with no dilution — 5.16:1 against the tile
measured_on_the_16px_raster.dot_at_16px: rgb(190,144,6), 2.74:1 against the tile beneath it — the weakest element in the icon, and deliberately so: it is a secondary detail in the original too, and the star is what carries the identity
measured_on_the_16px_raster.tile_against_a_light_tab_strip: 9.67:1 — the tile carries the shape there
measured_on_the_16px_raster.tile_against_a_dark_tab_strip: 1.66:1 — the tile nearly vanishes, but the star reads 8.59:1 against that strip, so the icon still resolves
measured_on_the_16px_raster.note_on_sampling: pixel (1,1) reads alpha 226, not 255. That is the corner arc being antialiased, not a transparency bug — rx 12.71 of 48 is ~4.2px at 16. Tile colours were therefore sampled at (8,1) and (1,8), which are fully opaque.
